outcome: Prevalence of hypothyroidism in infants born to hypothyroid mothers
cohort: 153 pregnant women with clinical hypothyroidism from the Endocrine Clinic in Qassim University, Saudi Arabia, between 2015 and 2019.
finding: The prevalence of hypothyroidism in infants born to hypothyroid mothers was 2.6%, while the prevalence of temporary/permanent hypothyroidism was 4.6%, with Cesarean delivery, gestational diabetes, and anemia being the most common maternal complications.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was the most common complication during pregnancy (26.8%).
